description:
Mount a sampling campaign testing the open conjecture that $\Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0] = 1/q + o(1)$ for uniform random square matrices over $\mathbb{F}_q$, using the packed bipedal permanent kernels.

## Background

[GGK2025] proves that a random $n \times k$ matrix over $\mathbb{F}_q$ (odd $q$, $k = O(\sqrt{n})$) fails to have full *permanental* rank with probability $\sim k/q^n$ — the probability of an all-zero column, and far below the determinantal analogue $\Theta(q^k/q^n)$ — and conjectures the square case: $\Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0] = 1/q + o(1)$, in sharp contrast with the determinant, where $\Pr[\det(A) = 0] = 1/q + \Omega_q(1)$ (for $q = 3$ the limit is $\approx 0.4399$ versus the conjectured $1/3$). [HKS2026] independently establishes that permanents of random matrices are significantly more uniform than determinants. For $q = 3$, [Scheinerman2024] §4 states the square case as Conjecture 4.1 and reports exact zero counts for $n \le 5$ plus Monte Carlo counts for $n = 6..30$ (declining from $10^{11}$ trials at $n \le 10$ to $10^6$ at $n = 30$); the proportions are statistically distinguishable from $1/3$ only for $n \le 13$. No published numerics are known for $q \in \{5, 7\}$, and the $n \ge 14$ drift region is unresolved.

The workspace's bipedal permanent kernels — built to reproduce and beat [Scheinerman2024] — provide $\mathrm{per} \bmod q$ evaluation for $q \in \{3,5,7\}$ across CPU and HIP/ROCm GPU backends; per-field coverage is uneven and the feasibility study's capability inventory is authoritative. Square-matrix sampling needs no new numeric kernels, though batch-level parallelism is harness-side. The rectangular validation targets the permanental-rank-deficiency event — every $k \times k$ row-submatrix permanent vanishing — and its baseline batches existing square kernels over row subsets; a dedicated evaluator is an optimization, not a prerequisite. Evaluation cost is Ryser's $\Theta(2^n n)$ per matrix, so the scientific reach in $n$ (how far the shape of the $o(1)$ term can be traced) is set by measured throughput and hardware budget. A published empirical convergence curve, supporting or contradicting $1/q + o(1)$, would be a citable contribution this toolkit is uniquely positioned to produce. The campaign proceeds only after a feasibility study fixes the attainable envelope and design.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A feasibility study documents the attainable sampling envelope (matrix sizes, sample counts, wall-clock and hardware budget) per field $q \in \{3, 5, 7\}$, measured on the existing CPU and GPU permanent paths, and closes with a go/no-go recommendation and campaign design.
- [hard] REQ-02: A sampling harness draws i.i.d. uniform matrices over $\mathbb{F}_q$, evaluates permanents in batches, and accumulates streaming zero-fraction statistics with confidence intervals; seeds, RNG choice, and versions are recorded for reproducibility.
- [hard] REQ-03: Empirical $\Pr[\mathrm{per}(A) = 0]$ curves versus $n$ for $q = 3, 5, 7$ over the feasible range, with confidence intervals, are published as a versioned dataset plus an analysis report assessing consistency with $1/q + o(1)$.
- [hard] REQ-04: The permanental-rank-deficiency predicate (all $k \times k$ row-submatrix permanents zero) is validated by exact enumeration and cross-implementation agreement on tractable $(q, n, k)$ cases, as an end-to-end correctness check of the pipeline.
- [aspirational] REQ-06: A preregistered rare-event estimator with demonstrated unbiasedness and interval coverage against exact cases estimates the deficiency probability toward the theorem's $\sim k/q^n$ regime.
- [aspirational] REQ-05: Convergence-shape characterization (parametric fit of the $o(1)$ term) and a permanental-versus-determinantal zero-fraction comparison figure.

## References

- [GGK2025] Ghasemi, Gross, Kopparty — Permanental Rank versus Determinantal Rank of Random Matrices over Finite Fields. APPROX/RANDOM 2025. arXiv:2512.03221; ECCC TR25-206.
- [HKS2026] Hunter, Kwan, Sauermann — Permanents of Random Matrices over Finite Fields. arXiv:2603.15856.
- [Scheinerman2024] Scheinerman — Fast Computation of Permanents over F_3 via F_2 Arithmetic. arXiv:2407.20205.
title: Empirical permanent statistics of random matrices over small prime fields
